title: METR's AI productivity study is really good
summary: Praises the METR RCT, which found experienced developers 19% slower while believing they were faster, and argues AI helps most outside one's comfort zone and when tired.

assertions.quote: But in fact they were 19% slower overall
developers came away from the study thinking they were 20% faster, but were in fact 19% slower.
Developers didn’t get faster with AI over the course of the experiment
the real niche of AI is when developers have to do tasks that are a little out of their comfort zone.
coding with AI requires less cognitive effort, and makes it easier to multi-task or just to zone out.
the screen-recording data showed that AI-assisted coding had more idle time
Working on a 500 line codebase is just qualitatively different from working on a 1M+ line codebase.
AI means I can work at times that I otherwise would be able to get nothing done at all
